main_text.p: ocymo, quibus in quibusdam nostris terris nihil vulgatius. Quidam farinam torrere solent, s in Pultis a- pulsem postea cogere: videoid mulis in locis ea- uenacea vulgatum, vt etiam tá aueide s alacriter vscen- ncom- tes ad efficandum meuna pellexerint. Verum moda, si melancholicum succum exinde generari, obstru- non pro- Hippocrates, vifcerum manife ste descrebendi atq, ob- bè fit pa- seruans in uis, qui largius s sapius eá sunt usi, rata. Cateant igitur sibi ab eiusmodi pulsibus, quibus Censura. humor melancholicus non expurgatur in sple- nem, vt propriam receptaculum, qui laborant calculo ventriculo, frigido. Cum laste, sale, s bui yro cenio so probant s quidam delicatio- res addunt saccharum: qui bui yro destinantur, loco eius usurpent: lardum, quod in stili vel sar- tagine torrendum est: quibus non inuisum est mel, possunt id permiscere, hæc enim singula essi- cunt, vt s secundus s salubrius edantur: hoc etiam modo parandæ sunt pultes ex ocymo, cato- ri, frumenti, quain vsum cibarium admi- Quidin- tentur. Inprimis vero hic opera danda, ne primis confistentia harum pulliculorum sit nimis cras- circa pul sa, descensa s compatta, sed mediocris, hæc enim tes obser ratione s mantus ventriculum s valenter alunt, uandum. nimis crasse, solidaq, meatus obstruunt, difficul- Præcepit, terq, concoquuntur: Sic vero consigerit, ut s fame- non cō- licus quispiam ex aliorum eduliorum defectus temnen- crassiorem quam parcitur, deuorant, s largiore dum. vini haustu eam imbuat. ita enim condensatio dissoluetur, prohibitum prohibeat, si nelentore tunc ad- bere-

page.notes: Scan is a faded, skewed photograph of a 16th–17th century Latin medical text; many words are doubtful and this is a best-effort transcription. Long s rendered as s. Marginal and right-column text is largely illegible at this resolution; the left-margin note "Cenfura" appears to be a marginal running label and was not reliably read. The right margin has one short note not legible enough to copy. Several lines near the bottom (right column, "bere-") are cut off by the page edge. Bottom-of-page text is partially hidden. Some Latin is likely misread; reading is not guaranteed for each word.
